result.markdown: --- title: >- [chunker.MarkdownChunker]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Chunk Markdown documents into overlapping segments at semantic boundaries. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/raghilda/blob/docs-embedding-providers/src/raghilda/_chunker.py#L64-L396){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python chunker.MarkdownChunker( chunk_size=1600, target_overlap=0.5, *, max_snap_distance=20, segment_by_heading_levels=None ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} This chunker divides Markdown text into smaller, overlapping chunks while intelligently positioning cut points at semantic boundaries like headings, paragraphs, sentences, and words. Rather than cutting rigidly at character counts, it nudges cut points to the nearest sensible boundary, producing more semantically coherent chunks suitable for RAG applications. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [chunk_size]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1600]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Target size for each chunk in characters. The chunker attempts to create chunks near this size, though actual sizes may vary based on semantic boundaries. Default is 1600 characters. [target_overlap]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.5]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Fraction of overlap between successive chunks, from 0 to 1. Default is 0.5 (50% overlap). Even with 0, some overlap may occur because the last chunk is anchored to the document end. [max_snap_distance]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[20]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum distance (in characters) to move a cut point to reach a semantic boundary. If no boundary is found within this distance, the cut point stays at its original position. Default is 20. [segment_by_heading_levels]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : List of heading levels (1-6) that act as hard boundaries. When specified, no chunk will cross these headings, and segments between them are chunked independently. For example, `[1, 2]` ensures chunks never span across h1 or h2 headings. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} The example below chunks a short Markdown document with a deliberately small `chunk_size` so the splitting is easy to see. With `segment_by_heading_levels=[1, 2]`, no chunk crosses an `h1` or `h2`, so each section is chunked on its own: ::: {#c70bea3c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from raghilda.chunker import MarkdownChunker chunker = MarkdownChunker( chunk_size=100, target_overlap=0.2, segment_by_heading_levels=[1, 2], ) text = '''# Introduction This is the introduction section with some content. ## Background Here is background information that provides context. ## Methods The methods section describes our approach. ''' chunks = chunker.chunk_text(text) for chunk in chunks: print(f"[{chunk.start_index}:{chunk.end_index}] {chunk.text[:40]}...") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [0:68] # Introduction This is the introduction ... [68:137] ## Background Here is background informa... [137:192] ## Methods The methods section describes... ``` ::: ::: Each printed line shows a chunk's character span (`start_index:end_index`) and the start of its text. To chunk a whole document instead of a bare string (preserving its `origin` and metadata), use `chunk()`, which returns a `ChunkedDocument`. ## Notes {.doc-notes} The chunking algorithm works as follows: 1. Parse the Markdown to identify semantic boundaries (headings, paragraphs, sentences, lines, words) 2. If `segment_by_heading_levels` is set, split the document at those headings first 3. For each segment, calculate target chunk boundaries based on `chunk_size` and `target_overlap` 4. Snap each boundary to the nearest semantic boundary (preferring headings > paragraphs > sentences > lines > words) 5. Extract chunks with their positional information and heading context
